description: Three fallback candidates (en-US, en, fr) whose failures are structurally DIFFERENT, so the retained cause is identifiable by type and by message. The en-US entries fail through the PhoneticResolver (which always throws the sentinel 'sentinel-resolver-alpha'); the en entries fail either through a library-generated type mismatch (a String where Gender is required) or through the same resolver under a DIFFERENTLY NAMED generated placeholder, so a same-type pair is still distinguishable by the contextualized message. Fragment.First adds a third failure kind: an en-US expression-fragment placeholder over a poisoned operand, which raises the library's own ExpressionEvaluationException, paired against an en entry that fails through the resolver. Two keys pair an alternatives-only entry (NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE, no cause) with a resolver-failing entry in both orders, so the policy is consulted once with a null cause and once with one. The instance policy is any-failure so every candidate is reached by default and a per-call override can narrow it. Two loaded locales share 'en', so tiebreakers is mandatory and lists exactly en-US and en.

Fragment.First.commentary: An expression-fragment placeholder. With a non-numeric badCount the comparison raises ExpressionEvaluationException, a library type that contextualization preserves rather than converting.

Mixed.NoMatchFirst.commentary: Alternatives-only with a false predicate: NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE with NO cause, so the first policy consultation carries a null cause.

Article.commentary: Fails with IllegalArgumentException when personGender is a String, giving the en candidate a cause of a different TYPE from the resolver's.
